dedupe_keys.name: groundwater variability and coseismic liquefaction hazards a case study from the 2014 south napa earthquake

description: Groundwater variability and coseismic liquefaction hazards: A case study from the 2014 South Napa Earthquake is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Michael Greenfield, Greenfield Geotechnical LLC (greenfieldgeotechnical.com). Both soil behavior classification and groundwater depth play major roles in the assessment of coseismic liquefaction. Prior research has established that layer thickness and arrangement of liquefaction-susceptible soils influences liquefaction manifestation at the ground surface. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project with 1 top-level file. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-6mvd-6b69. Keywords: groundwater variability, liquefaction hazard, Gaussian process regression, temporal groundwater model. Published 2026-09-18. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
